newsitem.title: san marino: SOCCER-BERGKAMP STRIKES TWICE IN 6-0 ROMP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BERGKAMP STRIKES TWICE IN 6-0 ROMP.

text.p: Former European champions The Netherlands routed San Marino 6-0 on Wednesday in a World Cup qualifier to maintain their lead in group seven.
The Dutch have 15 points from six matches, followed by Belgium, 3-1 winners over Turkey, who have 12 and a game in hand.
A poor first half did not produce a goal until the 40th minute, Dennis Bergkamp scoring. He turned away from his marker Mauro Valentini and shot the ball under goalkeeper Federico Gasperoni.
The Dutch finally got to grips with the game as the San Marino amateurs tired, five goals pouring through their defence in the final 27 minutes.
Aron Winter made it 2-0 with a shot from just outside the box. Pierre van Hooijdonk, in the 70th, and Frank de Boer, four minutes later, scored with headers.
Five minutes before time John Bosman, who was making his international comeback after a two-and-a-half year absence, made it 5-0 from close range.
Bergkamp's second goal of the match in the final minute took his international tally to 32, three short of the Dutch record held by Faas Wilkes.

Bergkamp, who travelled to San Marino by car because of his fear of flying, said: "We won and that is the most important thing. It is very difficult to play well here as San Marino don't play and only defend."
Coach Guus Hiddink admitted the Dutch were below par. "It was a poor game," he said.
